industry: Retail bakeries, custom cake boutiques, cupcake shops, and artisan bread bakeries (on-premise bake / take-home)
words_and_claims_to_avoid: 'Gluten-free', 'allergen-free', 'nut-free' without meeting the real standard and kitchen controls (FDA gluten-free labeling 21 CFR 101.91 for labels; FTC substantiation for ads)
Disease/medical claims ('cures inflammation', 'diabetic-safe miracle') without competent scientific support — high FTC/FDA risk
'Fresh daily' if product is frozen/thawed or not baked that day
'Organic' without compliant organic certification for the claimed products
'Up to 25% off' that almost never reaches 25%
compliance_notes: FTC Act s.5 + Health Products Compliance Guidance: food ads must be truthful and substantiated; health claims need competent reliable evidence; FTC defers heavily to FDA labeling standards for food health claims.
FDA 21 CFR 101.91: 'gluten-free' on labels means <20 ppm and no prohibited gluten ingredients — ads implying the same should be able to meet it.
Allergen statements: do not promise 'allergen-free kitchen' if shared equipment creates cross-contact risk — disclose honestly.
16 CFR 233/251: cake $ off, cupcake BOGO, complimentary tasting thresholds need clear conditions.
No medical cure claims for bakery foods.
Coupon fine print: end dates, exclusions (wedding cakes vs sheet cakes), and one-per-customer rules beside the offer.
standing_rules: Emotion-agnostic: joy, anticipation, belonging, relief are fine when they fit and stay legal.
Every angle and emotion_by_offer combo carries sell_the_outcome_line.
Vendor ROI labeled agency-only unverified; never print as fact on a client card.
Prefer one clear offer + one real photo + one QR (roofing-round5 directional) unless client insists on a coupon grid.
Leave thin industries thin — do not invent studies or pad gold.
